orientation_convention:
- Pose: "portrait stick" — long axis (v, 47.92 mm) vertical in the user's view; short axis (u, 28.4 mm) horizontal. [citation: geometry summary, board_context]
- BOTTOM edge := the v-max short edge, i.e. the USB-C cable edge. This is a functional anchor, not a geometric convenience: it is the only edge a mate enters from, and the control cluster (SW1/SW2) sits beside it. [citation: geometry J1 @ v-max + "Buttons SW1/SW2 beside it", board_context]
- Cable mate direction: the USB-C plug approaches along the −v direction, entering from beyond the v-max edge; the receptacle mouth opens through the board edge, not through a face. [citation: geometry J1 placement, board_context]
- TOP edge := the opposite short edge (v-min). Presumed module/antenna end by devkit convention — unconfirmed by the summary; treat as open until the module footprint position is extracted. [citation: geometry summary, board_context]
- FRONT (what the user sees) := the component face carrying the WROOM-32E module, SW1/SW2, SOT-223, and J1 body; this is the face toward the user both when the board is plugged castellated/breadboard-style (board vertical) and when it lies on a desk. [citation: geometry summary + README breadboard/castellated excerpt, board_context]
- REAR := the opposite face; implied bare/flush-seating for breadboard use, but NOT stated — verify in the board 3D model before using it as the resting plane. [citation: README excerpt, board_context]
- LEFT/RIGHT (−u vs +u): NOT derivable from the supplied summary. Pin it from the board silkscreen or a README photo before placing any asymmetric or mirrored feature; until then, side assignments are forbidden. [citation: lesson 6 veto, experiments/dspy-design.md L21]
user_facing_features:
1. USB-C port (J1) — end-wall window in the BOTTOM (v-max) end wall of the enclosure, centered at u ≈ 14.2 mm, spanning the 9.4..19.1 mm footprint plus plug-shroud clearance (typical USB-C plug overmold ≈ 10–12 mm wide); the user inserts the cable from outside along −v, i.e. from the bottom edge while facing the front. [citation: geometry J1 u 9.4..19.1 @ v-max edge, board_context]
2. Buttons SW1/SW2 — actuator openings on the FRONT face near the bottom edge, beside J1. Each maps to a distinct physical button (not interchangeable), so exact u/v offsets must be extracted from the board files before opening placement; the summary deliberately does not guess them. [citation: geometry "Buttons SW1/SW2 beside it", board_context]
3. WROOM-32E module / antenna zone — no opening, but a semantic surface: if the module sits at the TOP (v-min) end (unconfirmed), the top end wall and roof over it must stay RF-transparent (plain thin plastic, no metallic paint/shield). Open item: confirm module position along v. [citation: geometry "tallest parts" summary, board_context]
4. Castellated edge pads — a user-facing feature in the README's declared "castellated use" mode: the user solders through the board edges into a host PCB. An enclosure must either leave the edge pads reachable or be designed as a carrier; side walls that permanently bury the castellations contradict the documented use intent even if all booleans pass. [citation: README excerpt, board_context]
5. Non-feature constraint worth stating: NO mounting holes — the enclosure captures the board by outline rails/friction, never by screws, so nothing in the user's view depends on hole access. [citation: geometry "NO mounting holes", board_context]
